Toureendarby Polka

The Boys of the Lough play this on their 2002 album ‘Lonesome Blues and Dancing Shoes’ and call it “Curragh Races Polka”. It is in fact a polka version of the reel “The Curragh Races” (https://thesession.org/tunes/1760)

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 5th, 2013.

Toureendarby Polka

“…It is in fact a polka version of the reel ”The Curragh Races“…”

Mmm. Well, perhaps not; Kenny has pointed out - quite rightly - that there are not enough similarities to pair this tune with “The Curragh Races”, and the B part of the tunes are in fact quite different, so ignore that part of my post. Sorry, guys.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 5th, 2013.

There’s Worse Than That Around

I first heard this tune at a concert of the Band Cuas from Dingle (Méabh Ní Bheaglaoich - accordion, Liam Stapleton - Flute, Matt Griffin - Guitar), seems to be one of the polkas indigenous to the Dingle area (but I’m not an expert on this :)). It can also be found on the album Ragairne by Séamus Begley and Jim Murray.

↳ Posted by Clare on October 13th, 2013.

Re: Toureendarby Polka

Toureendarby (officially spelled Tooreenderby) is a place near Newmarket, Co. Cork – a well-known goldmine of Sliabh Luachra polkas. It is also home to the North Cork accordion legend Timmy O’Connor whose CD, full of rare local gems, is incidentally called ‘As It Was in Toureendarby’. Timmy would most likely be the oldest source living source of the polka, one of the many tunes that had been learned from him and then spread around, some becoming associated with completely different areas and musicians. He plays it in E dorian.

Curiously, I’m not sure where the alternative spelling ‘Taureen Derby’ comes from, since the search loops back to The Session and several recordings under that name. Timmy’s band The Monks of the Screw recorded the tune in 1991 as ‘Toureendarby Polka’. Funnily enough, Timmy doesn’t play it on the track, but he sure loves playing it in real life.

↳ Posted by Bregolas on February 8th, 2023.
